skill.name: project-min-evaluation
skill.description: Run existing project quality scripts before reporting completion or committing, using the detected package manager and stopping at the first failure.
skill.summary: Verify project quality with ordered checks and honest reporting of failures, missing scripts, and unverified scope.
skill.author: c3sc0-v4113

content.value_statement: Completion reports can overlook failing checks or untested changes. This skill guides ordered execution of existing project scripts and reports failures, missing checks, and unverified scope.
actual_capabilities: Select the package manager from packageManager metadata or supported lockfile signals.
Discover existing lint, typecheck, format:check, test, doctor, check, and conditional test:e2e scripts.
Run checks in the prescribed order and stop at the first failure.
Report passed, failed, missing, and unavailable checks with commands, errors, and unverified scope.
Handle conflicting lockfiles and scope package-level workspace checks to changed packages.
Treat doctor score regressions and new warnings as failures.
limitations: Requires an assistant with repository access and command execution permissions.
Uses existing package.json scripts and does not create missing quality checks.
Unavailable databases, browsers, or other services can prevent verification.
Does not sandbox or establish the safety of repository-defined scripts.

use_cases.title: Verify an implementation before handoff
use_cases.description: Run available quality checks and identify any unverified scope before reporting a feature as complete.

use_cases.title: Check a workspace change before commit
use_cases.description: Run root checks and relevant package checks for touched workspace packages before committing.

use_cases.title: Review verification evidence
use_cases.description: Request exact failing commands, errors, and unavailable checks to assess whether a change is ready for review.

prompt_templates.title: Run basic quality checks
prompt_templates.prompt: Use project-min-evaluation to run this repository's existing minimum quality checks. Report passed, failed, missing, and unavailable checks.

prompt_templates.title: Verify before committing
prompt_templates.prompt: Verify my changes before commit. Detect the package manager, run defined checks in order, and stop at the first failure.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate a failed check
prompt_templates.prompt: Run project-min-evaluation, diagnose the first failure, fix it within the change scope, and resume from that check. Report remaining unverified scope.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate a workspace behavior change
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this workspace change using root checks and checks for touched packages. Include test:e2e if behavior changed. Report lockfile conflicts and unavailable services.

output_examples.input: Verify a repository with passing lint, typecheck, and test scripts but no other quality scripts.
output: Formatting check, doctor, and aggregate check: not defined.
End-to-end tests: not defined; no end-to-end behavior changed.
Unverified scope: checks without defined scripts.

output_examples.input: Verify a change where the test script requires an unavailable local database.
output: Lint, typecheck, and formatting check: passed.
Tests: not run. Attempted command: npm run test.
Later checks: not run because test verification could not complete.
Unverified scope: database-dependent tests and remaining quality checks.

best_practices: Review repository script definitions and run them only in a trusted environment.
Resolve package manager conflicts before running checks.
Keep exact commands, errors, and unverified scope in the final verification report.
anti_patterns: Inventing commands for scripts that the project does not define.
Skipping a failing check to run later checks.
Reporting completion when required checks failed or could not run.

faq.question: Which assistants can use this skill?
faq.answer: The listing supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Running checks requires repository access and command execution.

faq.question: How does it choose the package manager?
faq.answer: The packageManager field takes priority. Otherwise, it uses pnpm, Bun, or npm lockfile signals, with npm as the fallback.

faq.question: What happens when multiple lockfiles exist?
faq.answer: Without packageManager metadata, it reports the conflict and asks which manager the project uses.

faq.question: Does it create missing quality scripts?
faq.answer: No. It reports missing scripts instead of inventing commands or adding configuration.

faq.question: When does it run end-to-end tests?
faq.answer: It runs a defined test:e2e script only when end-to-end behavior changed.

faq.question: What happens when a check fails or cannot run?
faq.answer: It stops progress through checks and reports the exact command, error, and unverified scope. Failed checks are fixed and rerun.
